samples.summary: `Array.isArray(thread.comments)` is false for a Yorkie array proxy, so `listThreads`/`findThread` reject every thread actually stored in the CRDT
samples.evidence: `listThreads` (comment-ops.ts:116) and `findThread` (:129) both gate on `!Array.isArray(thread.comments)` and skip/return-undefined when it fails. When the map comes from a live Yorkie root (`doc.getRoot().sheets[tabId].comments[id]`), `thread.comments` is a Yorkie ArrayProxy whose proxy target is a `CRDTArray`, not a JS array — this repo states that explicitly twice: worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:71 ("`Array.isArray`, which is false for a Yorkie array proxy") and worksheet-charts.controller.ts:68. Consequently, against a real document: `GET .../comments` returns `{threads: []}`, and `reply` / `PATCH` / `DELETE :threadId` / `DELETE :threadId/comments/:commentId` all 404 via `findThread`/`tabIdOfThread` (comments.controller.ts:463, :711). Every unit test in comments.controller.spec.ts / comment-ops.spec.ts feeds plain JS objects, so the whole feature passes CI while being non-functional in production. The frontend stores never use this guard — they use `Array.from(t.comments ?? [])` (yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:51), which works on the proxy.

samples.summary: `copyThread` detaches the anchor with `detachYorkieValue`, which corrupts array-valued anchor fields (`docs-range.posRange`, `pdf-text.rects`)
samples.evidence: comment-ops.ts:98 does `anchor: (detachYorkieValue(t.anchor) ?? {})`. `detachYorkieValue` branches on `Array.isArray` (yorkie-json.ts:168), which is false for a Yorkie array proxy, so nested arrays "come back as `{createdAt, movedAt}` CRDT metadata" — the repo's own words at worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:69-74 and worksheet-charts.controller.ts:66-70. Two of the four anchor shapes the controller advertises reading contain arrays: `DocsRangeAnchor.posRange` is a `TreePosStructRange` tuple (frontend/src/types/comments.ts:31) and `PdfTextAnchor.rects` is `PdfRect[]` (:69). So `GET .../comments` on a `doc` document — explicitly a supported operation per the controller docblock — returns every thread with `anchor.posRange` replaced by CRDT metadata, and likewise `rects` for PDF text threads. The frontend deliberately avoids this: pdf-comment-store.ts:56-70 copies `rects` field-by-field and yorkie-comment-store.ts:81-88 documents that `posRange` must not be round-tripped through JSON at all. The unit test only exercises a `pdf-region` anchor (plain nested object, no array), so it cannot catch this.

samples.summary: `applySetResolved` unconditionally `delete`s `resolvedAt`/`resolvedBy` on reopen; deleting a key that is not present on a Yorkie object throws, so `PATCH {resolved:false}` on a never-resolved thread can 500
samples.evidence: comment-ops.ts:214-224 runs `delete thread.resolvedAt` / `delete thread.resolvedBy` whenever `resolved === false`, with no existence check. Yorkie's object proxy `deleteProperty` routes to `CRDTObject.deleteByKey` → `RHTPQMap.deleteByKey`, which raises `fail to find <key>` when the key was never set. samples.summary: Notification `preview` is the raw comment body, so `@[username](userId)` mention tokens leak into the recipient's inbox instead of `@username`

samples.summary: New tab delete/duplicate paths gate on truthiness of `root.tabs[tabId]`, which a Yorkie proxy answers with a function for `toJSON`/`getID`/`toString` — writing a junk tab or attempting a delete of a non-key

samples.summary: `worksheetOrThrow` truthiness check lets a proxy method name through as a "tab", so `PUT .../tabs/toJSON/images` reports 200 while writing nothing

samples.summary: `addSlide` silently accepts an unknown `layoutId` and builds the slide from the first built-in layout instead
samples.evidence: `addSlide` passes `layoutId` straight to `MemSlidesStore.addSlide`, whose `resolveLayout` (slides/src/store/memory.ts:172-174) falls back to `getLayout(layoutId)`, and `getLayout` (slides/src/model/layout.ts:196-198) is `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS.find(...) ?? samples.summary: `applySlideChange` move can call `moveAfterByIndex(-1, from)` when `moveFront` is absent
samples.evidence: slide-ops.ts:118-125: the `to === 0` branch is only taken when `slides.moveFront` also exists. If an array-like exposes `moveAfterByIndex` and `getElementByIndex` but not `moveFront`, `to === 0` falls through `else if (to > from)` (false, since `from > 0` here) into `else { moveAfterByIndex(to - 1, from) }` = `moveAfterByIndex(-1, from)`, an out-of-range previous index. samples.summary: `deleteComment`/`deleteThread` raise their 404 from *inside* `doc.update`, the pattern the sibling images controller explicitly warns against
samples.evidence: comments.controller.ts:416-429 calls `applyDeleteComment` inside the `mutate` callback that `mutateMap` runs within `doc.update` (:451-454, :466-468), and throws `NotFoundException` from there for an unknown `commentId` — a routine 404, not an exceptional case. worksheet-images.controller.ts:87-90 states the opposite rule for the same reason: "Checked *before* `doc.update` rather than inside it: throwing from within the update leaves an aborted change on a document this request should not have touched at all." Yorkie discards its clone and rethrows on a throwing updater, so this is recoverable rather than corrupting, but it makes a plain 404 force a full document re-clone and diverges from the convention the change itself documents.

samples.summary: Sheet thread creation resolves the tab with a truthiness check on the Yorkie proxy, turning a bogus tab id into a 400 about row/column ids rather than a 404

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described and reachable. Backend `planCommentNotifications` assigns the raw comment body to `preview` (comments.controller.ts:550, :572, :588) while the frontend equivalent pipes it through `mentionBodyToPlainText` (notify.ts:35-37, used at :73, :92, :108; mentions.ts:124-130 maps `@[name](id)` -> `@name`). The path is live — the controller's `notify()` calls the planner and `createFromComment` on agent/API comment writes (comments.controller.ts:179-188) — and for `comment_mention` the leak is guaranteed, since that plan is only emitted when the body contains a mention token (:559-573). No upstream guard blocks it: `tabId` is a bare route param (tabs.controller.ts:167,236), the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:65-72) does not validate native-typed params, and `assertSheetDocument` only checks document type. finding.summary: Comment author is `username: undefined` for every API-key caller (the primary consumer of these routes)
finding.evidence: `author()` builds `{ userId: String(req.user.id), username: req.user.username }`. For API-key auth the request user comes from `packages/backend/src/api-key/api-key.strategy.ts:22-27`, which returns only `{ id, workspaceId, scopes, isApiKey }` — there is no `username` (only the JWT strategy sets one, `packages/backend/src/auth/jwt.strategy.ts:39-44`). So every thread/reply/resolve made with an API key (the CLI/agent path this feature exists for) writes `username: undefined` into the CRDT. Yorkie rejects `undefined` values on assignment, so this is likely a 500 on the write; if it does get stored, every API-authored comment and `resolvedBy` renders with no author in the editor. The controller docblock claims "an API key resolves to the user who minted it" — only the id does; the username is never loaded from the user table.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `author()` unconditionally builds `{ userId: String(req.user.id), username: req.user.username }`, storing `username: undefined` for API-key callers. The actual code at packages/backend/src/api/v1/comments.controller.ts:134-160 does the opposite: it only uses `req.user.username` when `typeof req.user.username === 'string' && req.user.username.length > 0` (the JWT case), and otherwise loads the row via `this.userService.user({ id: userId })` and uses `user.username`, throwing BadRequestException if the minting user was deleted. `photo` is only assigned when truthy, so no undefined value is assigned into the CRDT either. The reviewer is correct that api-key.strategy.ts:22-27 returns no username, but that is exactly the branch the guard covers. All three write paths (createThread :255, reply :340, setResolved :371) route through this single `author()` helper, so there is no bypassing call site. The controller docblock at :123-133 documents this as the fix for that precise bug, and comments.controller.spec.ts:392-410 (API-key request shaped exactly as the strategy returns, spec.ts:19) asserts the username is resolved from the User row ('ada-from-db'), with :413-420 and :424-425 covering the JWT and deleted-user cases. The described code is not present as claimed.

finding.summary: `copyThread` shallow-spreads the anchor, so nested CRDT proxies (PDF `rect`, docs `posRange`) leak into the HTTP response instead of plain JSON
finding.evidence: `anchor: { ...t.anchor } as AnyAnchor` copies nested values by reference. For a PDF thread the anchor is `{ kind, pageIndex, rect: {...} }` and for a docs thread `{ blockId, posRange, quotedText }` — the nested objects stay live Yorkie proxies. The repo's own equivalents avoid exactly this: `packages/frontend/src/app/files/comments/pdf-comment-store.ts:51-70` ("a spread would carry live proxy objects out of the CRDT, which is the bug this whole copy layer exists to prevent") copies field by field, and `packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-charts.controller.ts:61-72` documents that a spread makes `res.json()` fail or double-encode. This fires on `GET /comments` (list), `PATCH /comments/:id` and the reply/resolve responses for pdf and doc documents — i.e. the anchor a client needs to place the thread comes back double-encoded or crashes serialization. The sheet-cell anchor (flat strings) is unaffected, which is why the unit tests miss it.

verdict.reason: The quoted line does not exist in the cited file. `copyThread` at packages/backend/src/yorkie/comment-ops.ts:95-106 sets `anchor: (detachYorkieValue(t.anchor) ?? {}) as AnyAnchor` — not `{ ...t.anchor }`. `detachYorkieValue` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts:149-182) is a fully recursive walk: it maps arrays through itself (line 169) and rebuilds objects via Object.fromEntries/Object.entries recursing into each child (lines 176-181), never touching `toJSON`, so nested `rect`/`posRange` are detached as plain values with no double-encoding. The docblock at comment-ops.ts:83-94 explicitly documents choosing this over a spread for exactly the PDF `rect` / docs `posRange` reason, and comment-ops.spec.ts:170-190 asserts the PDF `rect` is deep-copied (`copy.anchor.rect).not.toBe(rect)`). The only downstream spread, comments.controller.ts:701, operates on the already-detached copyThread output (comments.controller.ts:316) and is gated to `kind === 'sheet-cell'` (line 693), the flat-string anchor the finding concedes is unaffected; the pdf/doc paths (comments.controller.ts:286, :486) return `copyThread(...)` directly. The matching shallow spread exists only in a different package/file, packages/frontend/src/components/comments/mem-comment-store.ts:133, which is not the named location and is a non-CRDT in-memory store.

finding.summary: `unwrapJson` on a whole worksheet uses bare `JSON.parse`, so duplicating a tab whose grid contains a control character (a multi-line cell) throws a 500
finding.evidence: `const worksheet = unwrapJson<Worksheet>(root.sheets?.[tabId]);` — `unwrapJson` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts:7-19) calls the proxy's `toJSON()` and then plain `JSON.parse`. The same file documents that Yorkie's raw JSON string path emits *unescaped control characters inside string values*, which is precisely why `parseJsonSnapshot`/`escapeControlCharsInJson` (lines 93-110) exist. A cell value containing a newline or tab is ordinary spreadsheet content, so `POST /tabs/:tabId/duplicate` would throw `SyntaxError` out of the withDocument callback and 500 instead of duplicating. Previous `unwrapJson` call sites only unwrapped small chart/image records; this is the first one that unwraps an entire user-authored grid.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `unwrapJson` uses bare `JSON.parse`, so a worksheet containing a control character (multi-line cell) would throw a SyntaxError and 500 on `POST /tabs/:tabId/duplicate`. The code is not as described. `unwrapJson` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts:14-30) calls the proxy's `toJSON()` and then `parseJsonSnapshot(str)` at line 22 — not `JSON.parse` — inside a try/catch that falls back to `detachYorkieValue(value)` (line 24), a JSON-free proxy walk. `parseJsonSnapshot` (lines 109-121) catches a SyntaxError whose message includes 'control character' and reparses via `escapeControlCharsInJson` (lines 43-102), which escapes \n, \t, \r, \b, \f and other <0x20 chars inside string literals while tracking quote/backslash state. The helper's docblock (lines 7-12) documents this exact multi-line-cell scenario, and yorkie-json.spec.ts:148-153 asserts `unwrapJson` on a proxy returning `{"cells":{"A1":{"v":"one\ntwo"}}}` with a literal newline yields the right object; :155-158 covers the unparseable fallback. The call site at tabs.controller.ts:249 uses this same import (line 29). So the described crash path does not exist.

finding.summary: Every per-slide op replaces the whole `root.slides` array, so concurrent edits to *any* slide between read and write are lost — the opposite of what the docblock claims
finding.evidence: `apply()` reads the deck (`readSlidesRoot(doc.getRoot())`), computes a new array outside `doc.update`, then assigns `root.slides = result.slides` wholesale. Yorkie resolves that as last-write-wins over the entire array, discarding any element/text change a collaborator committed on any slide in the interval. The class docblock says these verbs "each rewrite only `root.slides`" so "every concurrent edit in between" is preserved — only edits to `meta`/`themes`/`layouts` are. `writeSlidesRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:83-92) states the destructive contract explicitly; this path silently inherits it while documenting the opposite.

verdict.reason: The described defect does not exist in the code. `apply()` in slides.controller.ts:186-191 does NOT assign `root.slides = result.slides`; inside `doc.update` it obtains the live array (`const slides = root.slides as unknown as SlideArrayLike`) and calls `applySlideChange(slides, result.change)`. The only whole-array assignment there is `if (!root.slides) root.slides = []` (line 187), which fires only when the field is absent, so nothing can be lost. `SlideOpSuccess` has no `slides` field at all — it is `{ ok: true; change: SlideChange; id? }` (slide-ops.ts:53-59), and each op returns a granular change (slide-ops.ts:170, 189, 207, 221). `applySlideChange` (slide-ops.ts:92-133) lands it as one `splice`, or for a move uses the CRDT array's in-place `moveFront`/`moveAfterByIndex` (slide-ops.ts:118-125). The destructive `writeSlidesRoot` (slides-tree.ts:93-110) is not reachable from this controller: grep shows its only production call site is docs-content.controller.ts:238 (the whole-deck `PUT /content` route), and slides.controller.ts imports only `readSlidesRoot` (lines 19-22). The docblock's claim of granular, concurrency-preserving writes therefore matches the implementation rather than contradicting it.
